macro: The Fed held its policy rate at 3.50%-3.75% at the July 29-30 meeting in a 9-3 vote, with new Chair Kevin Warsh describing inflation as 'elevated' relative to the 2% goal even as three members dissented in favor of a cut. Core PCE has run at 3.3% year-over-year and headline CPI at 3.5%, keeping the door open to a hike rather than a cut later this year. Geopolitically, markets are watching reports that Iran-U.S. peace talks may resume this week after a temporary halt to strikes, which would ease pressure on oil and shipping. The week's data slate includes JOLTS Tuesday, ISM Services Wednesday, and the single most important release: Friday's July jobs report (Aug 7), the last major labor read before the Fed's September 16 decision.

energy: WTI crude is trading near $84.67 a barrel, up 1.29% in its most recent session, while Brent sits close to $88, up 1.2% Friday and capping a roughly 24% gain in July, its strongest monthly rise since March. The EIA's latest report (released July 29, for the week ending July 24) showed U.S. crude inventories fell 7.2 million barrels to 404.5 million, 7% below the five-year average. The Strait of Hormuz has remained effectively closed to shipping since March amid the Iran conflict, and while OPEC+ has added roughly 940,000 barrels a day of quota since the war began, insurance and crew availability continue to constrain actual throughput.
vix_and_dollar: The VIX's most recent close was 15.99 (July 31), down 6.44% on the day and sitting in the 15-20 'normal' band after a sharper spike the prior week. The Dollar Index (DXY) is near 99.72, down about 0.19% in the latest session, a mild softening that tends to support risk assets and dollar-priced commodities like gold, consistent with today's calmer volatility reading.
mortgage_rate: The 30-year fixed mortgage rate averaged 6.66% in Freddie Mac's July 30 survey, up from 6.58% the week before. The uptick works against the recent improvement in affordability — Zillow estimates falling rates and rising incomes had added roughly $30,000 to the typical household's home-buying power over the past year — and comes as existing home sales fell 2.4% in June to a 4.09 million annualized pace.
personal_finance_deep_dive: The average American carrying a credit card balance now owes $7,886, up 2.8% from $7,673 a year ago, even as average APRs sit near 21%. The gap traces back to a savings rate that has fallen to 4.0% in Q1 2026 from 6.2% in early 2024 — income has kept rising, but housing and everyday costs have absorbed most of the gain, leaving households increasingly reliant on revolving credit to bridge the difference. Lower- and middle-income households carry the largest share of this balance growth, since they have the least room to absorb a rate near 21% without cutting spending elsewhere.
wealth_building_deep_dive: Fidelity counted a record 665,000 retirement savers with 401(k) balances above $1 million last quarter, while Vanguard's separate data shows the average participant account hit a record $167,970 in 2025, up 13% for the year. The common thread across both datasets is consistency: savers who stayed invested through 2025's volatility and kept contributing on autopilot — rather than trying to time entries and exits — are the ones showing up in these record counts. A concrete step this week: check whether your plan offers auto-escalation (an automatic annual bump to your contribution rate) and turn it on if you haven't already; it is the single easiest way to replicate the saving behavior behind these records.
